cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: I’ve been meaning to ask you for some advice about restaurants.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: I need to book somewhere to celebrate my sister’s 30th birthday, and I liked the sound of that place you went to for your mum’s 50th.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: The Junction. Yeah, I’d definitely recommend that for a special occasion. We had a great time there. Everyone really enjoyed it.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Where is it again? I can’t remember.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: It on Grayson Street only about a two walk from the station.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Oh that’s good I prefer not to have to drive anywhere but I don’t want to have to walk too far either.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Yes, the location’s perfect, but that’s not necessarily why I’d recommend it.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: The food’s amazing.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: If you like fish, it’s probably the best restaurant in town for that.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: It’s always really fresh and there are lots of interesting dishes to choose from But all the food is good there.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Is it really expensive?

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: It’s certainly not cheap, but for a special occasion I think it’s fine It’s got a great atmosphere and before dinner you can go up on the roof and have a drink It’s really nice up there, but you need to book It’s very popular as the views are spectacular.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Sounds good. So that’s definitely a possibility then. Is there anywhere else you can think of?

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: If you want somewhere a bit less formal, then you could try Paloma.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Where’s that? I haven’t heard of it.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: No, it’s quite new. It’s only been open a few months, but it’s got a great reputation already. It’s in a really beautiful old building on Bow Street.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Oh, I think I know where you mean. Right beside the cinema.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Yes, that’s it. I’ve only been there a couple of times, but I was really impressed. The chef used to work at Don Felipe’s, apparently. I was really sorry when that closed down.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: So is all the food they serve Spanish, then?

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Yeah. You can get lots of small dishes to share, which always works really well if you’re in a group.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Hmm. Worth thinking about.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Yeah. There’s a lively atmosphere and the waiters are really friendly. The only thing is that you need to pay a £50 deposit to book a table.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: A lot of restaurants are doing that these days. I should have a look at the menu to check if there is a good choice of vegetarian dishes. A couple of my friends have stopped eating meat

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Not sure I say the selection of those would be quite limited.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions five to ten. Now listen and answer questions 5 to 10.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: I’ve just thought of another idea. Have you been to the Audley?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: No, don’t think I’ve heard of it. How’s it spelt?

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: A-U-D-L-E-Y. You must have heard of it. There’s been a lot about it in the press.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: I don’t tend to pay much attention to that kind of thing. So where is it exactly?

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: It’s in that hotel near Baxter Bridge, on the top floor.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Oh, the views would be incredible from up there.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Yeah, I’d love to go. I can’t think of the chef’s name, but she was a judge on that TV cookery show recently. And she’s written a couple of cookery books.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Oh, Angela Frayne.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: That’s the one. Anyway, it had excellent reviews from all the newspapers.
